title: Does the host draw with wgpu directly or through a toolkit?
body:
The host has to draw a grid of character cells for every pane, pixel regions
over some of them, and its own chrome: pane borders, a session switcher, a
status line. The TUI rule means the chrome is cells too. This decision is
what the host draws with.

## Options

| Option | Grid alignment | Pixel regions | What it brings |
|---|---|---|---|
| wgpu directly, own glyph atlas | Exact, by construction | A second textured pass | A renderer we own, a few hundred lines |
| egui on wgpu | Approximate; its text layout is proportional first | Through a paint callback | Widgets the TUI rule forbids anyway |
| iced | Approximate, same reason | Through a custom shader widget | The Elm architecture, again mostly unused |
| gpui | Good; built for an editor | Through custom elements | A widget layer the protocol replaces, and an API that moves with Zed |

A cell-grid renderer is small and well understood: a monospace glyph atlas,
one instanced quad per cell, one pass for backgrounds, one for glyphs, one
for pixel regions. Every terminal emulator is one. Shaping and rasterising
come from a crate, `cosmic-text` or `swash`, which also covers font fallback
and emoji inside a monospace grid.

A toolkit brings text layout and widgets. Under the TUI rule the host uses
neither: its widgets are cells. What is left of a toolkit is the window and
event loop, which `winit` gives on its own.

## Lean

wgpu directly. A toolkit would sit between the grid and the screen and fight
it for alignment, and the thing it adds is the thing the design forbids.

## Cost

- The host owns font loading, atlas management and cell metrics. These are
  solved problems with reference code in every terminal emulator, but they
  are ours to maintain.
- No toolkit means no free input widgets: a text field for the chat pane is
  written against the grid.

## Open

- Whether `libghostty`'s renderer is usable on its own, which would make the
  grid renderer a dependency rather than a module. Its public surface as of
  this writing is the VT parser, `libghostty-vt`; this needs checking before
  any renderer code is written.
- Which shaping crate. `cosmic-text` does shaping and fallback together;
  `swash` is lower level.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/618aab71
notes.text: Open again after decade became a nested Wayland compositor on 2026-11-06. smithay renders with its own GLES2 renderer and imports client buffers through EGL. wgpu's stable API cannot import a Wayland dmabuf, so the likely outcome is that the cell renderer moves to smithay's GL renderer. The grid, font and atlas code in `grid.rs` and `text.rs` stay; the pipeline in `gpu.rs` and `cell.wgsl` would become a GLSL shader. The lean is now whatever smithay's winit backend hands us. The spike settles it.
